label: early original-phase p/q/u/1 input after an earlier p/q/j/y
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at positions t=1..5 (peak at t=2-3, about 88% of mass at t=2..4). It never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. Which token is input matters: p and q have the highest rates (about 6x lift each, together about 47% of mass), then u and 1 (about 3x), then g, y, b, f. Earlier tokens also matter: firing is stronger when p/q (and to a lesser extent j/y) appeared at a previous step or as the first token. The strongest activations are repeated p/q runs near the start (e.g. p p p, p p q). It also leans toward first occurrences (in_first lift 1.5x). The magnitude is graded and spread over many tokens, so it acts like an accumulated early-sequence p/q signal rather than a crisp token detector. The predicate catches about 57% of mass on dev but with low precision (about 0.30), so this is only a partial explanation.
